Short title extent and commencement

THE
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may be called the Balochistan
Village Ordganization Ordinance, 1990.
(2) It extends to the
whole of the Province of Balochistan except tribal areas.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Ordinance to override other laws

THE
THE
ALL PAKISTAN LEGAL DECISIONS
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
2. Ordinance to override other laws.‑‑The
provisions of this Ordinance shall have effect notwithstanding anything
contained in any other law, or instrument having the force of law, for the time
being in force.

Definitions

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
3. Definitions.‑‑In this Qrdinance, unless there is
anything repugnant in the
subject or context;
(a) "Bye‑laws" means the bye‑laws made
under this Ordinance.
(b) "Government" means the Government of
Balochistan;
(c) "Prescribed" means prescribed by Rules;
(d) "Project"
means a scheme meant for the economic welfare, development and uplift of one or
more than one resident of a village or of more than one adjacent villages;
(e)
"Registrar" means a person appointed to perform the duties of a
Registrar of Village. Organizations under this Ordinance and includes an
Additional Registrar, Joint Registrar or Deputy Registrar;
(f) "Rules" means
rules made under this Ordinance;
(g) "Schedule
Bank" rneans the scheduled bank which has been declared under section 37
(2)(a) of the State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956 (XXXIII of 1956);
(h) "State Bank"
means the State Bank of Pakistan;
(i) "Village Organization"
means an Organization registered under subsection (2) of section 5.

Appointment of registrar

THE

CHAPTER II

4. Appointment of Registrar.‑‑(1) The Government shall
appoint a person to be the Registrar of Village Organizations for the whole
province or any part of ii and may appoint a person or persons to be Additional
Registrar, Joint Registrar or Deputy Registrar by general or special order,
confer on any such person all or any of the powers of Registrar, Additional
Registrar, Joint Registrar or Deputy Registrar under this Ordinance.
(2) Notwithstanding
anything contained in subsection (1) the Government may, instead of making
appointments referred to in subsection (1), direct that all or any of the
powers conferred and imposed upon the Registrar shall he exercised and
performed by such officer or officers and within such local limits, as the
Government appoints in this behalf.

Formation registration etc of a village organisation

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER II
REGISTRATION AND
INCIDENTAL MATTERS
5.Formation Registration, etc. of a Village Organization.‑‑(l)
Subject to subsection (5), any seven or more individuals, including women,
actually residing in the same village or adjoining village may, by subscribing
their names and signatures to an application in the prescribed form, form a
Village Organization and submit the same in duplicate to the Registrar for
registration of Village Immunization.
Explanation.‑‑A declaration by the signatories of the
application contained in the application to the effect that each of them is
actually residing in the same village or villages adjoining one another or each
other shall be final and binding on the Registrar.
(2) The Registrar, on
receipt of the application referred to in subsection (1), shall register the
Village Organization and issue a certificate to that effect and every such
certificate shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that ail the requirements
of this Ordinance in respect of registration have been complied with.
(3) The registration of
a Village Organization shall bind the subscribers thereof to the same extent as
if they respectively had signed the bye‑laws and contained a covenant on
their part, their heirs and legal representatives to observe and be bound by
all the provisions of the bye‑laws subject to the pro‑visions of
this Ordinance and all moneys payable by any subscriber to the Village Organization
under the bye‑laws shall be a debt due from him to the Village
Organization.
(4) From the date of
registration mentioned in the certificate of registration, the signatories of
the application together with such other persons as may from time to time become
subscribers, shall be a body corporate by the name contained in the Certificate
of Registration, capable forthwith of exercising all the functions of a Village
Organization and having perpetual succession and shall, by the said name, sue
and be sued.
(5) Every Village
Organization shall intimate to the Registrar in writing of change, if any, in
its address last intimated to the Registrar.

Limited liability

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER II
REGISTRATION AND INCIDENTAL MATTERS
6. Limited liability.‑‑The liability of a subscriber shall
be limited to the
amount of subscription laid
down in the bye‑laws.

Powers of the registrar

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER II
REGISTRATION AND INCIDENTAL MATTERS
7. Powers of the
Registrar.‑‑(1) Every Village; Organization shall send to
the Registrar by registered
post;
(a) List of the
members of its Managing Committee immediately on this election;
(b) a change in
the list referred to in clause (a) or in the list of subscribers subsequent to
the registration of the Village Organization immediately on the occurrence of
such change; and
(c) its annual
accounts within three months of the close of the accounting year;
(2) The
Registrar shall hold a special general meeting of a Village Organisation within
one month or receipt by him of a requisition in writing of at least one‑fifth
or the number of subscribers of the Village Organisation, provided the Managing
Committee has earlier failed to hold such meeting.
(3) The Registrar shall also
exercise the powers and perform the functions and duties entrusted to him by or
under this Ordinance or any other law for the time being in force.

Subscribers not to have interests in the assets of a village organisation

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER II
REGISTRATION AND INCIDENTAL MATTERS
8. Subscribers not to have
interests in the assets of a Village Organisation.‑‑No individual
by becoming a subscriber of a Village Organisation shall have, or be deemed to
have, any title or interest in the assets of the Village Organisation or its
assets for recovery of subscriptions or donations made by him nor shall the
same be liable to attachment or sale under any decree or order or any Court,
tribunal or other authority in respect of any debt or liability incurred by
such subscriber.

Service of documents on a village organisation and authentication of documents and proceedings

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER II
REGISTRATION AND INCIDENTAL MATTERS
9. Service of documents on a
Village Organisation and authentication
of documents and proceedings.‑‑(l) A document may be served on
a Village Organisation by sending it to the Village Organisation at its
registered address by post under a certificate of posting or by registered post
or by delivering it to the Chairman or Secretary of the Managing Committee at
the address of the Village Organisation last recorded by the Registrar.
(2) A document or proceeding
requiring authentication by a Village Organisation may be signed by the
Chairman or Secretary of the Managing Committee.

Prior claim of a village organisation

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER III
PRIVILEGES OF VILLAGE ORGANISATIONS
10. Prior claim of a Village
Organisation.‑‑Subject to any prior claim of the Federation or
Province in respect of land revenue or any money recoverable as arrears of land
revenue or of a land owner in respect of rent or any money recoverable as rent,
any debt or outstanding demand owing to a Village Organisation by any
subscriber or past subscriber shall be a first charge on the assets of the
subscriber and shall also be recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
Explanation.‑‑For the purposes of this section, (a)
subscriber shall include any other person liable for the payment of any debt or
outstanding demand owing to a Village Organisation; and (b) the Village
Organisation shall issue a certificate stating the debt or outstanding demand
owing to it from the subscriber, whether under any agreement or other document
or otherwise howsoever, as at any given date and such certificate shall be
conclusive evidence of the debt or outstanding demand owing to the Village
Organisation as final and binding accordingly.

Application of banker's books evidence act

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER III
PRIVILEGES OF VILLAGE
ORGANISATIONS
11. Application of Banker's
Books Evidence Act.‑‑The provisions of the Banker's Books Evidence
Act, 1891 (XVIII of 1891), shall apply to every Village Organisation as if it
were a bank or banker within the meaning of that Act.

Exemption from stamp duty registration and Court fee etc

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER III
PRIVILEGES OF VILLAGE
ORGANISATIONS
12. Exemption from Stamp Duty, Registration and Court Fee etc.‑‑A
Village Organisation shall not be liable to the payment of any stamp duty under
the Stamp Act, 1899 (11 of 1899), any fee payable
under the Registration Act, 1908 (XVI of 1908), any court‑fee payable
under the Court Fees Act, 1870 (VII of 1870), and any other fee, rate, levy,
octroi, impost and tax, howsoever styled, leviable or chargeable by the
Government or any Local Authority under any provincial law on movable or
immovable properties, including their transfer and mutation, income, wealth,
profession or export and import of goods.

Channellisation of certain loans through village organisation

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER III
PRIVILEGES OF VILLAGE
ORGANISATIONS
13. Canalization of certain loans through Village Organisation:
‑From a date to be notified by the Government in the Balochistan
Gazette in consultation with the State Bank, no scheduled bank operating in
Balochistan Province shall extend loans and advances as defined in the Banking
Companies Ordinance, 1962 (LVII of 1962), for agricultural production and
development to the subscribers of a Village Organisation except through the
Village Organisation to which they are subscribers.

Amalgamation or transfer of village organisation

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER III
PRIVILEGES OF VILLAGE
ORGANISATIONS
14. Amalgamation or transfer of
Village Organisation.‑‑(l) Any two or more adjoining Village
Organisations may, by resolution passed by a three‑fourth majority of the
subscribers present at a special general meeting of each such Village
Organisation held for the purpose, amalgamate themselves into a single Village
Organisation:
Provided that
each subscriber has had clear 15 days written notice of the resolution and the
date of meeting. The resolution of the Village Organisations concerned shall,
on such amalgamation be a sufficient convenience to vest the assets and
liabilities of the amalgamating Village Organisations in the amalgamated
Village Organisation.
(2) Any Village Organisation
may, by a resolution passed in accordance with the procedure laid down in the
subsection (1), transfer its assets and liabilities to any other adjoining
Village Organisation which is prepared to accept them:
Provided that when any such
amalgamation or transfer of assets and liabilities involves the transfer of its
liabilities by any Village Organisation to any other adjoining Village
Organisation, it will not be made without giving three months notice to the
creditors of both or all such Village Organisations.

Funds of village organisations and their investment

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER IV
PROPERTY AND FUNDS
OF VILLAGE ORGANISATIONS
15. Funds or Village
Organisations and their investment.‑‑(1) The funds of Village
Organisation shall consist of‑‑
(a) admission fees of
subscribers
(bl subscriptions of and
donations from subscribe
(c) grants from the Federal or a Provincial
Government, a Local Authority or a Corporation owned or controlled by the
Federal or a Provincial Government, or from a foreign Government or
Organisation or an International Organisation with the prior concurrence of the
Federal Government;
(d) donations from the public including
firms, companies and trade bodies; and
(e) loans
and advances raised by it.
(2) A
Village Organisation may invest its surplus funds:
(a) in a Government Savings
Bank; or
(b) in any
of the securities specified in section 20 of the Trusts Act, 1882 (II of 1882);
or
(c) with any scheduled bank; or
(d) in
any other mode permitted by the Rules.

Borrowing power

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER IV
PROPERTY AND FUNDS
OF VILLAGE ORGANISATIONS
16. lfi. Borrowing
power.‑‑A Village Organisation may, for the purposes of its
functions, borrow from a subscriber, scheduled bank, a financial institution or
any other person.

Restriction on voluntary winding up

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER V
LIQUIDATION AND ARBITRATION
17. Restriction on voluntary winding up.‑‑No Village
Organisation shall wind up itself voluntarily.

Winding up

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER V
LIQUIDATION AND ARBITRATION
18. Winding up.‑‑If
the Registrar, on receipt of an application made by three‑fourths of the
subscribers of a Village Organisation present at a special general meeting
called for the purpose or if the number of subscribers is reduced to below
seven, is of opinion that the Village Organisation ought to be wound up, he may
issue an Order directing it to he wound up, and when necessary, may appoint a
salaried officer of the Government or any Court or of a Union or District
Council as a Liquidator for the purpose without any additional remuneration.

Power of liquidator

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER V
LIQUIDATION AND ARBITRATION
19. Power of liquidator: ‑A liquidator appointed under section 18
shall have the power with sanction of the Registrar to do all or any of the
following things:
(a) to pay any class or classes
of creditors in full;
(b) to make any compromise or
arrangement with creditors or persons claiming to be creditors or having or
alleging themselves to have any claim, present or future, whereby the Village
Organisation may be rendered liable;
(c) to compromise all debts,
and liabilities capable or resulting in debts, and all claims, present or
future, certain or contingent, subsisting or supposed to subsist between the
Village Organisation and a debtor or persons apprehending liability to the
Village Organisation and all questions in any way relating to or
affecting the assets or the
discharge of any such liability, debt, or claim and give a complete discharge
in respect thereof;
(d) from time to time to
determine the contribution or subscription to be made or remaining to be made
by the subscribers or past subscribers or by the estates, heirs or legal
representatives of deceased subscribers or by any officer to the assets of the Village
Organisation, such contribution or subscription including debts due from such
subscribers or persons;
(e) to institute and defend
suits and other legal proceedings on behalf of the Village Organisation in the
name of his office.
(1) to issue requisitions under
section 27 upon the Collector for the recovery as arrears of land revenue of
any sum ordered by him to be recovered as dues from subscribers or as a
contribution or subscription to the assets of the Village Organisation or to
the cost of liquidation;
(g) to get disputes referred to
arbitration;
(h) to investigate all claims
against the Village Organisation and, subject to the provisions of this
Ordinance, to decide questions of priority arising out of such claims, and to
pay rateably according to the amount of such debts, the surplus, if any, being
applied in payment of interest or return from the date of liquidation at a rate
to be fixed by the Registrar not exceeding the contract rate;
(i) to sell the movable and
immovable property and actionable claims of the Village Organisation by public
auction or private treaty with power to transfer the whole thereof to any
person or to sell the same in parcels;
(j) to raise on the security of
the assets of the Village Organisation any
money requisite;
(k) to determine by what person
and in what proportion the cost of the liquidation shall be borne;
(1) to give such directions in
regard to the collection and distribution of the assets of the Village
Organisation as may appear to him to be necessary for winding up the affairs of
the Village Organisation;
(m) to fix the time or times
within which creditors shall prove their debts and claims or be included for
the benefit of any distribution made before those debts or claims are proved;
(n) to carry on the business of
the Village Organisation as may be necessary for the beneficial winding up of
the same:
Provided that no liquidator
shall determine the contribution or subscription, debt or dues to be recovered
from a past subscriber or the representative of a deceased subscriber unless
opportunity has been given to such past subscriber or to such representative to
answer the claims:
Provided further that all debts
due to the Federation or Province shall have priority over all debts which are
not secured by a mortgage, charge or lien on the property of the Village
Organisation or any part thereof but nothing herein contained shall affect the
provisions of the Balochistan Land Revenue Act, 1967 (XVII of 1967) or any
other law relating to land revenue in force in the area;
(o) to do all such other acts
and things as may be necessary for the winding up of the affairs of the Village
Organisation.

Dissolution of a village organisation

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER V
LIQUIDATION AND ARBITRATION
20. Dissolution of a Village Organisation.‑‑When the
affairs of a Village Organisation have been completey wound up or when the
Registrar is of the opinion that the official liquidator cannot be appointed,
or proceed with the winding up of the Village Organisation, for want of funds
and assets or any other reason whatsoever and it is just and reasonable in the
circumstances of the case that an order of dissolution of the Village
Organisation be made, the Registrar shall make an order that the Village
Organisation be dissolved from the date of the order, and the Village
Organisation shall be dissolved accordingly:
Provided that such dissolution
shall not extinguish any right of, or debt due to, the Village Organisation
against or from any person.

Disposal of surplus assets on dissolution of a village organisation

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER V
LIQUIDATION AND ARBITRATION
21. Disposal of surplus assets
on dissolution of a Village Organisation.‑‑On the dissolution of a
Village Orgianisation after its liabilities have been met, its surplus assets
shall not be divided among its subscribers but they shall be at the disposal of
the Registrar for transfer or distribution, as the case may be, to such other
Village Organisation or Organisations as in the opinion of the Registrar are
nearest in terms of distance to the dissolved Village Organisation.

Power of registrar to assess damage against delinquent promoters etc

BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
BALOCHISTAN STATUTES
ORDINANCE I OF 1990
BALOCHISTAN VILLAGE
ORGANIZATIONS ORDINANCE, 1990
CHAPTER V
LIQUIDATION AND ARBITRATION
22. Power of Registrar to assess damage against deliquent promoters, etc.‑ (1)
Where, in the course of the winding up of a Village Organisation it appears
that any person who has taken part in the organisation or management of the
Village Organisation or any past or present chairman, secretary, other member
of the Managing Committee or other officer of the Village Organisation has
misapplied or retained or become liable or accountable for any money or
property of the Village Organisation or has been guilty of misfeasance or
breach of trust in relation to the Village Organisation, the Registrar may, on
the application of the liquidator or of any creditor or subscriber or of his
own motion, examine into the conduct of such person and make an order requiring
him to repay or restore the money or property or any part thereof respectively
with interest or return at such rate as the Registrar thinks just or to
contribute such sum to the assests of the Village Organisation, by way of
compensation in regard to the misapplication, retainer, misfeasance or breach
of trust as the Registrar thinks just;
Provided that no order under
this section shall be passed unless the person to be effected thereby is given
an opportunity of being heard.
(2) This section shall apply
notwithstanding that the act is one for which the offender may be criminally
responsible.
